Research / methods

Evolutionary forecasting

Leveraging evolutionary principles to forecast future states of large noisy systems

All research↗

Overview

Evolutionary forecasting applies principles from evolutionary theory to predict the future states of complex, dynamic systems. By treating systems as evolving populations subject to selection, drift, and mutation-like processes, we develop robust predictive models that account for uncertainty and adaptation in noisy environments.

Questions we explore.

01

Adaptive Forecasting Models

Developing prediction frameworks that evolve with changing system dynamics and learn from forecast errors

02

Population-Level Predictions

Forecasting aggregate behaviors in large systems by modeling individual-level variation and selection pressures

03

Evolutionary Game Theory

Predicting strategic interactions and equilibria in competitive environments using evolutionary dynamics

04

Phylogenetic Forecasting

Using evolutionary relationships and historical patterns to predict future trait evolution and system trajectories

05

Noise-Robust Prediction

Developing forecasting methods that maintain accuracy despite high levels of stochasticity and measurement uncertainty

Methods & perspective.

We combine evolutionary algorithms, Bayesian inference, and machine learning to create forecasting systems that adapt to changing conditions. Our methods incorporate fitness landscapes, selection gradients, and evolutionary constraints to generate predictions that account for both deterministic trends and stochastic variation.

Research directions

Market Evolution Forecasting

Predicting financial market dynamics by modeling trading strategies as evolving populations competing for resources

Pathogen Trajectory Prediction

Forecasting viral evolution and epidemic spread using phylodynamic models and evolutionary constraints

Adaptive Climate Models

Developing evolutionary forecasting approaches for ecological systems responding to environmental change
